title: 2026-11-04_Linux.Mirai_Incident_Response_5c2
description: Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity on the victim host. Your task is to investigate the compromised system, identify the malware behavior, and respond to the incident.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity on the victim host. Your task is to investigate the compromised system, identify the malware behavior, and respond to the incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the victim host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter the passkey 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the victim host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter the passkey 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity of periodically collecting `/etc/passwd`, home directory listings, and sensitive files, then exfiltrating them to a C2 server.
levels.solution:
1. Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.
2. Look for unfamiliar service names or misspellings of legitimate services.
3. Use `systemctl status <service>` to check the status and description of each service.
4. The service responsible for the suspicious activity is likely named `dvrHelper.service`.
5. The final flag is `dvrHelper.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual descriptions or startup behavior.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the ExecStart path in the service configuration to identify the suspicious activity.

levels.title: Determine Communication Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system for exfiltrating data to a C2 server. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Use `systemctl cat dvrHelper.service` to view the service configuration.
2. Pay particular attention to the ExecStart line, which specifies the path to the script launched by the service.
3. The script contains the port number to establish communication with the C2 server.
4. The port number is `5556`.
5. The final flag is `5556`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat dvrHelper.service` to view the service configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the ExecStart line in the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is specified in the script launched by the service.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigators suspect that a mechanism keeps the suspicious service running across reboots and process termination. Determine which system component is responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. Use `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.
2. Look for timers associated with the suspicious service.
3. The timer responsible for recurring unauthorized execution of the suspicious service is named `dvrHelper.timer`.
4. Verify the timer configuration using `systemctl cat dvrHelper.timer`.
5. The final flag is `dvrHelper.timer`.
